proof_natural:
**Proposition.** For any quantum system S with Hilbert space H, there exists no function v: O → ℝ that assigns predetermined values to all observables O ∈ B(H) such that: (1) v(A) ∈ σ(A) for all A ∈ O, and (2) for any orthonormal basis {|ψᵢ⟩} spanning a subspace, if A = Σᵢ aᵢ|ψᵢ⟩⟨ψᵢ|, then exactly one v(|ψᵢ⟩⟨ψᵢ|) = 1.

*Proof.* We assume that quantum systems are described by complex Hilbert spaces H with dim(H) ≥ 3, observables are self-adjoint operators in B(H), and measurement outcomes must lie in the spectrum σ(A) of observable A. Let v be a hypothetical value assignment function defined on all observables simultaneously, and suppose that for any complete set of orthogonal projectors {Pᵢ} with ΣᵢPᵢ = I, exactly one projector has value 1.

Consider a 3-dimensional subspace of H with orthonormal basis {|e₁⟩, |e₂⟩, |e₃⟩}. Such a subspace exists since dim(H) ≥ 3. Define the projectors Pᵢ = |eᵢ⟩⟨eᵢ| for i = 1,2,3.

We now invoke the Kochen-Specker theorem, which provides an explicit construction of 117 vectors in ℝ³ with specific orthogonality relations. Map each Kochen-Specker vector vᵢ ∈ ℝ³ to a quantum state |ψᵢ⟩ = Σⱼ vᵢⱼ|eⱼ⟩ via the natural linear isomorphism between ℝ³ and span{|e₁⟩, |e₂⟩, |e₃⟩}. This mapping preserves inner products: ⟨ψᵢ|ψⱼ⟩ = vᵢ·vⱼ, so each orthogonal triple in the Kochen-Specker configuration maps to mutually orthogonal quantum states.

For each orthogonal triple {|ψᵢ⟩, |ψⱼ⟩, |ψₖ⟩}, the corresponding projectors Pᵢ = |ψᵢ⟩⟨ψᵢ|, Pⱼ = |ψⱼ⟩⟨ψⱼ|, Pₖ = |ψₖ⟩⟨ψₖ| satisfy Pᵢ + Pⱼ + Pₖ = I₃ by the completeness relation for orthonormal bases in the 3-dimensional subspace. By our assumption, exactly one of v(Pᵢ), v(Pⱼ), v(Pₖ) must equal 1 for each such triple.

The crucial property of the Kochen-Specker configuration is that it contains overlapping triples—certain vectors appear in multiple orthogonal triples. When we attempt to assign values 0 or 1 to each projector consistent with the constraint that exactly one projector in each triple has value 1, the overlapping structure leads to a contradiction. The Kochen-Specker theorem guarantees that no consistent assignment exists.

Therefore, no value assignment function v can exist satisfying our requirements. This theoretical impossibility is corroborated by experimental observations: the Zeeman effect demonstrates that atomic energy levels split differently depending on magnetic field orientation, while the Stark effect shows that electric fields mix atomic states with observable properties depending on field configuration. These phenomena exemplify the context-dependence that our proof establishes must exist.

This completes the proof. □
